in_hebrew.name: תיאודורלה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: תיאודורלה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו במילים היווניות 'תיאוס' (אלוהים) ו'דורון' (מתנה), ומשמעותו 'מתנה אלוהים' או 'שׂרה אל'. השם נמצא בשימוש בקרב קהילות נוצריות שונות ומשקף את הקשר בין השם לבין האמונה הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Θεοδωρέλα
in_greek.long_meaning: Θεοδωρέλα προέρχεται ἀπό τὰ ελληνικὰ λόγια 'Θεός' (Θεο-) καὶ 'δῶρον' (-δωρέλα), ὁπόταν σημαίνει 'δωρεὰ Θεοῦ' ἢ 'χάρισμα ἀπὸ τὸν Θεόν'. Ὁ ὄνομα Θεοδωρέλα εἶναι σύνθετος μορφή τῆς λέξεως Θεοδώρα, ποὺ σημαίνει τὴν ἄνω ἔννοια.

in_latin.name: Theodorella
in_latin.long_meaning: Theodorella derivatur ex vocabulis Graecis 'theos' (Deus) et 'doron' (donum), significans 'Donum Dei' vel 'Gift of God'. Nomen hoc in usu est inter communitates Christianas et reflectit nexum inter nomen et fidem Christianam.

in_english.name: Theodorella
in_english.long_meaning: Theodorella originates from the Greek words 'theos' (God) and 'doron' (gift), meaning 'Gift of God' or 'Divine Gift'. This Christian name reflects the belief in God as the giver of all good things. Historically, names with the 'theos' prefix were common in early Christian communities, signifying a direct connection to the divine. Theodorella, as a feminine form related to Theodore, embodies the spiritual significance of being a blessing or gift from God. The name carries connotations of divine favor and grace, making it a meaningful choice for Christian families.

historical_references.reference: Theodora, a Byzantine Empress (428-450 AD), was known for her strong will and her influence over Emperor Theodosius II. Her influence extended to religious matters, and she is credited with convincing her husband to restore the banished bishop of Ephesus, John Chrysostom, from exile. The name Theodorella may be a feminine derivative of Theodoros, a common masculine name during this period inspired by Theodora.

The name Theodorella may also have been inspired by Saint Theodora, a Christian martyr from the 3rd century AD, who was known for her faith and her strength in the face of persecution. Her story is described in various early Christian writings, including the Acts of Theodora and the Martyrdom of Theodora and Theocistus.
